summary: Capecitabine is an oral fluoropyrimidine prodrug of 5-fluorouracil used in colorectal and breast cancer. It carries a boxed warning for serious adverse reactions or death in patients with complete dihydropyrimidine dehydrogenase (DPD) deficiency (test for DPYD variants before starting) and for increased bleeding with concomitant vitamin K antagonists such as warfarin (markedly altered INR/bleeding, including death). Common toxicities include hand-foot syndrome, diarrhea, nausea, and myelosuppression. Take within 30 minutes after a meal and adjust dose for toxicity and renal impairment.
indications: Adjuvant treatment of Stage III colon cancer
Perioperative treatment of locally advanced rectal cancer (with chemoradiotherapy)
Advanced or metastatic breast cancer (single agent if anthracycline/taxane not indicated)
Metastatic breast cancer in combination with docetaxel after anthracycline failure

moa: Prodrug enzymatically converted (via carboxylesterase, cytidine deaminase, and thymidine phosphorylase - higher in tumor tissue) to 5-fluorouracil, which forms FdUMP (inhibiting thymidylate synthase and DNA synthesis) and FUTP (misincorporated into RNA), causing cytotoxicity in proliferating cells.

absolute: History of severe hypersensitivity to fluorouracil or capecitabine
relative: Concomitant vitamin K antagonists (warfarin) - intensify INR monitoring

preg: Can cause fetal harm based on mechanism and animal data (embryolethality/teratogenicity). Verify pregnancy status before starting; advise effective contraception during treatment and for 6 months (females) / 3 months (males) after the last dose.
lact: Do not breastfeed during treatment and for 2 weeks after the final dose due to potential for serious adverse reactions in the breastfed child.
renal: Contraindicated if CrCl <30 mL/min. For CrCl 30-50 mL/min, reduce starting dose to 75%. Monitor renal function; optimize hydration.
hepatic: Monitor patients with hepatic impairment more frequently for adverse reactions; hyperbilirubinemia may occur. Use caution.

major: Vitamin K antagonists (warfarin) - markedly altered coagulation/bleeding, including death (boxed warning); monitor INR frequently
Allopurinol - may decrease capecitabine efficacy; avoid concomitant use
minor: Antacids (aluminum/magnesium hydroxide) - small increase in exposure

pk: Rapid GI absorption; activation to 5-FU within hours
20-25 C, keep tightly closed; hazardous drug
pearls: DPYD testing recommended before starting - complete DPD deficiency can be fatal (boxed warning)
Marked, potentially fatal interaction with warfarin - monitor INR closely (boxed warning)
Hand-foot syndrome is the dose-limiting toxicity; pyridoxine and dose modification used
Oral 'self-administered 5-FU' - tumor-selective activation via thymidine phosphorylase
missed: If a dose is missed, do NOT take a make-up dose or double the next dose; skip the missed dose and continue the regular schedule. Contact the oncology team for guidance.
overdose: Acute manifestations include nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, GI irritation/bleeding, bone marrow depression; consistent with severe 5-FU toxicity. Management: supportive care, monitor and treat cytopenias, fluids; uridine triacetate is an antidote for fluoropyrimidine overdose/early-onset severe toxicity. Hospitalize and consult toxicology/oncology.
